findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the startup-binding staleness contract: confirm no MCP consumer/test relied on per-request config freshness, and record that config is intentionally frozen at server startup (or add a coverage note if refresh must be preserved).
evidence: 'Compose MCP config ONCE at server startup (a startup binding / operation snapshot) instead of calling load_config() per request'

Startup-composed binding is shared read-only state consumed by every per-request handler; absence rationale: plan does not state whether the binding tolerates or ignores mid-lifetime config changes previously observable via per-call load_config().
findings.finding: The plan changes MCP config from per-request load_config() (L422/591/735) to composed ONCE at server startup, which changes staleness semantics: config edits made after server start were previously picked up on the next request and will now be frozen at startup. The plan treats this as behavior-preserving (fingerprints 'equal except recorded deltas') but does not enumerate whether any consumer or test relied on per-request config freshness, nor state that no request-time config mutation is expected during a server lifetime.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (first): 'Compose MCP config ONCE at server startup ... instead of calling load_config() per request at mcp_server.py L422/591/735'
scenarios: A long-running MCP server whose config file/env is updated after launch: prior per-call behavior reflected the change on the next tool call; the once-at-startup binding serves stale config until restart, and a behavioral suite that never restarts mid-test would not catch the divergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to step 3 and the Compatibility section confirming MCP config is intentionally composed once per server lifetime (no mid-lifetime refresh contract) and that no consumer depends on per-request reload, or note the recorded delta if refresh semantics change.
